newsitem.title: USA: Pa. drafts bill to end electric monopolies - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. drafts bill to end electric monopolies - paper.

text.p: Pennsylvania officials are nearly finished drafting legislation to dismantle the state's electric monopolies, the Philadelphia Inquirer said Tuesday.

In its current form, the draft bill would allow electric companies to refinance high-cost nuclear plants with new bonds paid off by surcharges on consumer bills. The surcharges would expire in 2006 at the latest.
Beginning in 1999, companies would be free to compete on price, driving down prices.
The final hurdle for the bill is determining a method to protect the state Treasury from revenue losses as the cost of electricity falls, the paper said.
Lawmakers said a bill could be passed before the state Legislature adjourns later this month.
